target_customer: Engineering and SRE teams at software companies that run production services
problem: Incident response ran through manual Slack threads, spreadsheets and scattered tools, so teams were slow to coordinate, track and learn from outages.
business_model: B2B SaaS per seat subscription for incident management and on-call
product_category: Incident management and on-call, now AI SRE

founders.name: Quentin Rousseau
founders.background_notes: Early and first site reliability engineer at Instacart per the YC page; title shown as CEO in 2021 TechCrunch and CTO on the YC page.

founders.name: JJ Tang
founders.background_notes: Led product management at Instacart per the YC page.

competitors.name: FireHydrant
competitors.what: Incident management and response platform for SRE and DevOps teams
competitors.traction_then: Grew from 10 to 54 employees between May 2020 and August 2021
competitors.funding_then: 8M Series A in May 2020 and 23M Series B in August 2021

competitors.name: Blameless
competitors.funding_then: Backed by Lightspeed and Accel; 20M reported on emerging from stealth, date not confirmed

competitors.name: PagerDuty
competitors.what: Incumbent alerting and on-call platform that Rootly integrated with

technical_complexity.rationale: Deep Slack integration plus workflow automation and many third party integrations; standard SaaS engineering with some integration breadth.

defensibility.rationale: Embedded in incident workflows and data, but several funded rivals built similar Slack native products.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Atlassian later announced it was shutting down Opsgenie and Rootly marketed migrations; PagerDuty stayed a rival and Rootly itself acquired ThinkHive in July 2026.

market_need_then: Engineering teams at fast growing companies ran incidents by hand in Slack; FireHydrant and Blameless raised funding in 2020 and 2021 showing active demand.

branding.domain_note: Uses rootly.com; domain history not found.

identity.logo: Black and white wordmark variants with a brand page

branding.brand_signature: Humans of Reliability series and Rootly Supply merchandise
branding.community_and_virality: Humans of Reliability podcast (2025 to 2026), a merch store called Rootly Supply, and Rootly AI Labs, all listed on its site; no third party press on the brand found.

brand_strength.rationale: A distinctive name that hints at root cause, with community assets such as a podcast and merch, but no independent evidence it drove growth.

outcome_analysis: Rootly's founders came from Instacart's reliability team, raised a 3.2M seed at launch in July 2021 and a 12M Series A in August 2023. It reports use by many well known tech companies, placed in Deloitte's 2025 Fast 50 per a search summary, and bought ThinkHive in July 2026 to extend into AI reliability. Competition from FireHydrant, PagerDuty and incident.io remains intense.
notes: Seed confirmed by TechCrunch and the company blog; Series A confirmed by the company blog, TechCrunch and SiliconANGLE. Total raised stated by the company as 15.2M. No Series B found. Founder education not found. Blameless funding date unconfirmed, so its source_date is approximate. ThinkHive acquisition date July 2026 comes from PitchBook via search summary.
